## Summary

Micro-Star International (MSI) is a Taiwanese multinational based in New Taipei City, founded on 4 August 1986 and listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange [1]. Its lineup includes laptops, desktop computers, motherboards, graphics cards, monitors, servers and industrial PCs, and its subsidiary FUNTORO, set up in 2008, serves the vehicle infotainment market [1].

The registry spells the company nine ways across 23 MA-L blocks; Micro-Star INTL CO., LTD. holds ten of them and the rest are listed as aliases [2]. A MAC in an MSI block is most likely the wired or wireless interface of an MSI laptop, desktop or motherboard, but which network silicon MSI fits is not documented in the sources consulted [1].

MSI's NVD history is host-side rather than radio-side: a write-what-where in the motherboard firmware SMI handler, privilege escalation through the drivers of its MSI Center, Dragon Center and App Player utilities, and arbitrary memory access through the Afterburner RTCore driver [3]. FCC grantee codes are not listed because the FCC ID databases refused the session that wrote this entry, and msi.com refused it too; nothing is filled in from memory. Randomization is the host operating system's behaviour and is unknown here.
